"GAME DESIGN @COMMENT_BODY@ TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE SPECIFICATION: FORTRESS AFTERMATH 100

================================================================================
SECTION 1: CORE ENGINE, RENDERING @COMMENT_BODY@ CAMERA ARCHITECTURE
================================================================================
Create a hyper-detailed, first-person 3D voxel-hybrid sandbox fortress survival game set in a decaying, dynamic post-apocalyptic world.

1.1 FIRST-PERSON VIEWPORT @COMMENT_BODY@ CAMERA SYSTEM:
- True First-Person Body Awareness: Looking down renders the player's tactical arms, chest rig, legs, and dynamic shadow.
- Dynamic Field of View (FOV): Base 90° FOV; smoothly widens to 105° during sprint/slide; narrows dynamically per weapon optic (1.5x reflex, 4x ACOG, 12x variable thermal sniper scope) with dual-render Picture-in-Picture (PiP) scope glass refraction.
- Procedural View-Bobbing @COMMENT_BODY@ Sway: Multi-axis sinusoidal camera bobbing tied to footsteps, velocity, breathing stamina, and injury state. Weapon models exhibit realistic inertia, aim-down-sights (ADS) sway, collision push-back when approaching walls, and physical recoil kick.
- Post-Processing @COMMENT_BODY@ Shaders: Volumetric fog, dynamic day/night directional sun/moon lighting with real-time cascading shadows, screen-space ambient occlusion (SSAO), blood/mud/acid screen-edge splatter shaders, chromatic aberration during explosions, and night-vision/thermal post-process overlays.

1.2 PLAYER LOCOMOTION @COMMENT_BODY@ PHYSICS ENGINE:
- Movement Vectors: Full 360-degree ground movement (WASD / Virtual Dual-Thumbstick with dynamic deadzone) featuring variable walk speed, tactical sprint (Shift / Sprint Toggle) consuming stamina, crouch (Left Ctrl) reducing hitbox height by 50% and muffling footstep audio radius by 75%, and prone (Z) for low-profile crawl under 1-block gaps.
- Parkour @COMMENT_BODY@ Traversal: Momentum-based sprint-sliding, automatic 1-block step-up smoothing, active 2-block ledge mantling/vaulting with first-person hand-grab animations, and ladder/scaffolding climbing.
- Rigid-Body @COMMENT_BODY@ Ragdoll Physics: Realistic gravity, fall-damage calculation with ankle-sprain debuffs on high drops, knockback impulses from explosions/boss slams, and active physics interaction with debris.

================================================================================
SECTION 2: HUD, BOTTOM HOTBAR @COMMENT_BODY@ 1,000-ITEM INVENTORY ARCHITECTURE
================================================================================
2.1 BOTTOM-SCREEN HOTBAR (PRIMARY HUD):
- Visual Design: Anchored at the bottom-center of the screen, a sleek, semi-transparent dark-slate tactical dock with 10 distinct numbered slots (Keys 1–0, Mouse Scroll Wheel, or direct tap/click).
- Slot Telemetry: Each hotbar slot displays a crisp 3D isometric icon of the block or gun, item stack count (up to 999 for blocks), active durability bar (color-coded green-to-red), current magazine/reserve ammo counter, and a glowing active-selection border.
- Quick-Swap @COMMENT_BODY@ Wheel: Pressing Q toggles between the current slot and the previously equipped slot. Holding Middle-Mouse opens a radial quick-access sub-wheel for grenades, healing syringes, and repair wrenches.

2.2 FULL INVENTORY @COMMENT_BODY@ BLOCK CATALOG MATRIX (E / TAB):
- Layout: Full-screen translucent tactical overlay divided into Left (Player 3D Paperdoll, Armor Slots, Stat Readouts), Center (60-Slot Backpack Grid), and Right (Master 1,000-Block @COMMENT_BODY@ 100-Gun Blueprint/Creative/Crafting Index).
- Navigation Tools for 1,000+ Items:
  * Instant live-filtering Search Bar (searches by name, material, tag, or resistance type).
  * Multi-tier Category Tabs: [All], [Structural], [Traps @COMMENT_BODY@ Defense], [Electronics @COMMENT_BODY@ Power], [Interiors], [Terrain], [Pistols], [Shotguns], [SMGs], [Rifles], [Snipers], [Heavy/LMGs], [Explosives], [Energy/Sci-Fi], [Elemental], [Experimental].
  * Sort Filters: Sort by Durability, Blast Resistance, Fire Rate, DPS, Weight, or Alphabetical.
  * Seamless Drag-and-Drop @COMMENT_BODY@ Shift-Click: Drag any block or weapon directly onto the bottom

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete playable browser game based on the “Fortress Aftermath 100” post-apocalyptic fortress-survival specification.

## Requirements
- Implement a first-person voxel-hybrid survival game with movement, combat, scavenging, building, hotbar, and an extensive searchable inventory/catalog.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript game using Canvas raycasting rather than adding an engine or dependencies.
- Used a generated 1,100-item blueprint catalog and a 60-slot-style inventory UI as practical approximations of the requested scale.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the playable game UI and raycast environment, including movement, hostiles, shooting, health/stamina, pickups, barricade placement, and survival HUD.
- Added inventory, catalog search/categories/sorting, hotbar selection, medkits, reload, pause, and deployment screens.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/latest.jpg`.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- Browser automation via `playwright-cli` could not start because its Chromium install was missing; a system Chromium screenshot was successfully captured instead.

## Next Move
1. Continue refining or testing gameplay if desired; the implementation is present but is a lightweight prototype rather than the full requested 3D feature set.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: HUD, inventory, menus, and responsive styling.
- `game.js`: Canvas renderer, controls, gameplay, catalog, and inventory logic.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Most recent visual check.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Run locally with a static file server; Python server on port `3002` was used for the screenshot.

content.text:
Implemented a playable **Fortress Aftermath 100** browser-game prototype.

- `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js` provide a raycast survival game with movement, combat, scavenging, barricade placement, survival meters, hotbar, inventory, searchable 1,100-item catalog, and pause/deployment screens.
- Controls include **WASD** to move, **mouse** to look and fire, **Shift** to sprint, **Ctrl** to crouch, **E** to interact, **F** to build, **R** to reload, and **Tab** to open inventory.
- `node --check game.js` passed. I captured and inspected `screenshots/latest.jpg` using system Chromium; Playwright’s Chromium installation was unavailable.

This is a lightweight Canvas raycasting prototype rather than the full 3D engine and advanced rendering described in the specification.
